top_story.headline: Army-supporting intelligence task order gets a $152.8 million ceiling increase without competition
top_story.dek: The General Services Administration cites simultaneous conflicts and a new Secretary of War task force in raising the ceiling to $567.6 million.
paragraphs: The General Services Administration, acting for the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command's C5ISR Center, plans to increase the ceiling on its Global Operational Support, Information Insight, and Threat task order by $152,779,419, from $414,857,176 to $567,636,595, using a sole-source exception to fair opportunity. The task order was competitively awarded in May 2024 and runs through May 2029.

The justification says the work expanded because the United States is engaged in or supporting multiple simultaneous conflicts, including Ukraine and Iran, and because of domestic drone incursions in the northeastern United States. It also says the Secretary of War directed a new Joint Interagency Task Force 401, for which this task order was selected as a heavy contributor. The document states that earlier internal funding realignments are exhausted and that the agency is developing a competitive acquisition strategy for a new procurement.

Also today: Immigration and Customs Enforcement is adding a temporary detention structure in Batavia, New York, to an existing contract with Akima Infrastructure Protection, LLC (value redacted), and the Army ordered armed guard services in Erbil, Iraq, from GardaWorld Federal Services before posting its justification.

sections.headline: A $152.8 million ceiling increase for an Army-supporting intelligence task order, plus an immigration detention expansion, lead the sole-source list
paragraphs: 57 new sole-source justifications and 1000 new solicitations were posted October 7-8; none were repeats of earlier editions (83 amendments to already-listed solicitations are not repeated).
Nearly all of the sole-source justifications carry redacted dollar values, so the figures below appear only where the documents state them.

blocks.title: Army-supporting intelligence task order gets a $152.8 million ceiling increase without competition
meta: Vendor redacted in the document text
$152,779,419 ceiling increase

General Services Administration
blocks.text: The General Services Administration, buying for the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command's C5ISR Center, wants to raise the ceiling on its Global Operational Support, Information Insight, and Threat task order from $414,857,176 to $567,636,595 (a 36.83 percent increase). The justification cites simultaneous conflicts including Ukraine and Iran, domestic drone incursions in the northeastern United States, and a Secretary of War directive to stand up Joint Interagency Task Force 401. It also says earlier internal funding realignments are exhausted, and that the agency is meanwhile devising a competitive strategy for a replacement contract.

blocks.title: Immigration and Customs Enforcement adds a temporary detention structure in Batavia, New York, to an existing contract
meta: Akima Infrastructure Protection, LLC
value redacted
only one company can do it
Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement
blocks.text: Immigration and Customs Enforcement plans to modify an existing detention services contract with Akima Infrastructure Protection, LLC to add a temporary detention structure, medical and environmental support, and armed guards at its Service Processing Center in Batavia, New York, to house up to 100 detainees. The justification says the agency has an increased need for beds in New York because of changes affecting state and local detention space, and that using another vendor would duplicate costs and add security risk. The modification raises the contract's ceiling; the new figure is redacted.

blocks.title: Army orders armed guards for Erbil, Iraq, and justifies the sole-source choice after the fact
meta: GardaWorld Federal Services
value redacted
urgent need, no time to compete
Department of Defense (Army Contracting Command, Rock Island)
blocks.text: On behalf of U.S. Army Central and the Combined Joint Task Force for Operation Inherent Resolve, the Army issued a notice to proceed on September 10, 2026 and awarded an undefinitized task order to GardaWorld Federal Services for armed guard services near Erbil International Airport. This justification is post-award: it was written October 8, after work was already ordered under the multiple-award Global Protective Services contract. The Army cites an urgent need and a compressed 20-day mobilization window.

blocks.title: Immigration and Customs Enforcement buys 366 parking spaces near its Washington, D.C., headquarters from a single garage
meta: Potomac Center CF, LLC
value redacted
only one company can do it
Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement
blocks.text: Immigration and Customs Enforcement is awarding Potomac Center CF, LLC, at 550 12th Street SW, a 3.5-month base contract for 366 spaces in the Potomac Center South underground garage. The justification says the garage is the only location with a secure direct connection to the agency's headquarters and security modifications for emergency access, and that the agency faces an elevated threat environment including frequent protests around the building. It notes the services have not been procured before.

blocks.title: Transportation Security Administration extends a sole-source help desk task order after a protest forced a re-compete
meta: Quasars
value redacted
only one company can do it
Department of Homeland Security, Transportation Security Administration
blocks.text: The incumbent, Quasars, was awarded a five-year sole-source task order for the Online Learning Center help desk on August 20, 2026. After an agency-level protest, the Transportation Security Administration took corrective action to compete the work, and this modification shortens performance to no later than May 19, 2027 so the 70,000-user system keeps support in the meantime.

items: Department of Homeland Security — sole-source follow-on with the International Organization for Migration for services reuniting families covered by the Miss L. settlement; the prior contract ran through September 12, 2026 and the work stems from a 2021 court order; value not stated (70SBUR26P00000013).

Department of Defense — 60-day extension of Fort Carson, Colorado, base operations for incumbent T&H Services LLC while a Government Accountability Office protest (B-424583) of the successor contract holds up the new award; value redacted (W911RZ19C0002P0085).

Department of Defense — Navy financial-management data transformation work for KPMG, the vendor since September 2018; the Navy says switching would delay audit remediation by about 18 months; value redacted (N0018926FZ108).

Department of Homeland Security — interim sole-source operations and maintenance for the Visa Security Program Tracking System with Steampunk Inc. while the system moves to a new platform; value redacted (70CTD026FR0000055).

Department of Defense — Vigor Marine LLC gets added repair work on the USS Gabrielle Giffords (LCS-10) after damage was found in drydock; the justification says the hull damage could not have been identified earlier; value redacted (N00024-25-C-4409_A00039).

Department of Homeland Security — Immigration and Customs Enforcement buys Hootsuite Inc. social media platform and Talkwalker image-recognition tools for public affairs on a brand-name basis; value redacted (JA-26-0292).
National Aeronautics and Space Administration — $47,453,711 sole-source award to Omitron, Inc. for orbital safety analysis (collision avoidance) for agency spacecraft (80GSFC26D0010JOFOC).

Department of the Navy — presolicitation of a sole-source low-rate initial production contract to Raytheon Company for the Joint Multiple Effects Warhead System for Tomahawk missiles; the notice says Raytheon has been the Tomahawk developer and manufacturer since 1994 (N00019-26-RFPREQ-WPM280-0311).

U.S. Coast Guard — solicitation for the Homeland Security Cutter – Light Icebreaker, an indefinite-delivery contract for design and production of a new vessel class using a two-phase down-select (70Z02326R93280004).
U.S. Secret Service — solicitation for 9mm duty and training ammunition; proposals due October 26, 2026 (70US0926R70093976).

sections.headline: No new USAspending awards of $2 million or more, and none of $100,000 to $2 million, were found in this window
paragraphs: The USAspending sweep for September 13 to October 8, 2026 found no new contract awards over the $2 million threshold and none in the $100,000 to $2 million screen that were not already reported.

sections.headline: No new apportionment files approved in this window
paragraphs: No new apportionment files from the Office of Management and Budget were approved between October 3 and October 8, 2026. No changes were detected to federal spend plans during this period.

footer.coverage_window: October 7-8, 2026 (Pacific time) for SAM.gov; October 3-8, 2026 for OMB apportionments; a 25-day trailing sweep (September 13 to October 8) for USAspending contract actions.
